4 — plan-defect: leg (c) cannot pass with M1's view as written — `{selector: '#todo-0', text: 'buy milk'}` is unsatisfiable for any implementation of this task. `#todo-0` is the Checkbox root: `client/src/TodoItem.tsx` passes `render={<span id={`todo-${rowId}`} />}` so the id lands on `<span role="checkbox" aria-checked="false" aria-label="buy milk">`, whose textContent is empty — the todo's text is in the sibling `<span class="flex-1 …">`. `assertView`'s `text` is `element.textContent.includes(...)`, so the exam fails `convergence: view not satisfied / view #todo-0: no match has text "buy milk"`. Verified against the run's own dom.html. Everything before that view is green: the same spec with only `{selector: '#todoList li', count: 3}` resolves `ok: true` in-process under ULTRA_RUN_DIR, with walls.json carrying sync_ms and converge_ms and transitions.json carrying 3 entries. Two spellings that would pass, either of which the plan can pick: `{selector: '#todo-0', attr: {name: 'aria-label', value: 'buy milk'}}` (which is how `#todo-0` 'carries buy milk', as the Context puts it) or the persistence exam's own `{selector: '#todoList li', count: 3, text: 'buy milk'}`. I implemented M1 as written rather than working around it, since the spec literal leg (a) reads back is written by the peer's exam over this same path.
